newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asia needs 6-10 new satellites a year - executive.
newsitem.headline: Asia needs 6-10 new satellites a year - executive.

text.p: Asia needs between six and 10 satellites each year to keep up with the region's new media and telecommunications demands and to replace old satellites, an industry executive said on Monday.

According to current trends, Asia needs around 15 percent new capacity from satellites every year just to keep pace, Peter Jackson, chief executive of Hong Kong's Asiasat Telecommunications Ltd, told a telecoms conference.
"If we continue, it will require us to put in the air six to 10 satellites just for Asia every year," Jackson said.
Asiasat, which listed recently on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, now has two satellites over Asia and is planning to launch its third by the end of 1997.
But despite growth in the region's satellite business, Jackson did not predict that transponder costs would fall.
He said the advent of digital technology, which compresses information sent to the satellite, meant that customers would need to lease fewer transponders on each satellite.
